subquestions.text_open: 5.1.2 Using the coordination numbers obtained above, write the chemical formula of the crystal.
5.1.3 State the lattice type of the crystal.

5.2 Consider an ideal hexagonal crystal composed of X and O. The coordinates of three X atoms in the unit cell are (1/2, 1/2, 0), (0, 1/2, 1/3), and (1/2, 0, 2/3). The unit cell may be viewed as containing helical X-O-X-O chains extending along c. For example, when viewed along c, rotate the X atom at (1/2, 1/2, 0) clockwise by 120° about the line a = 1/3, b = 2/3 and then translate it upward by 1/3 of the c-axis length; it reaches (0, 1/2, 1/3). Applying the same clockwise rotation and upward translation to the X atom at (0, 1/2, 1/3) gives (1/2, 1, 2/3). Applying them once more gives (1/2, 1/2, 1), equivalent to (1/2, 1/2, 0). This is illustrated below; the numbers in the figure are the c-axis coordinates of the X atoms. 5.2.1 Call the helical sense described above left-handed. Correspondingly, a helix that rotates counterclockwise while advancing along c is called right-handed. The unit cell contains another helical chain whose axis lies at a = 2/3, b = 1/3. State whether this chain is left- or right-handed.

text_images.description: Schematic of the helical X-O-X-O chain, projected along c. The main outline is a solid parallelogram. Slightly left of center inside it is a solid black point surrounded by a circular path bearing three clockwise arrows. Three light-gray circles with black outlines are evenly spaced on this path. Their labels increase clockwise: "0" at the lower right, "1/3" at the lower left, and "2/3" at the top. At the lower left of the image is an axis legend: a horizontal right-pointing arrow labeled a, an arrow slanting up and left labeled b, and the letter c at their common origin.
